docs.title: Follow a specific trajectory
docs.text:
Joint level control involves directly controlling the angles or positions of the robot's individual joints. Each joint is treated as an independent actuator, and the control system sends commands to each joint to achieve the desired angles.

For this example we will not use joint level control but a different method called Task/Cartesian Level Control. Task or cartesian level control focuses on controlling the position and orientation of the robot's end-effector in a Cartesian coordinate system (X, Y, Z coordinates and orientations). In our robot leg case we don't have Z axes (or orientation) and our end-effector is foot (end of our robot leg).

In this example we will follow a circle trajectory i X,Y plane. We defined that trajectory with our function generate_circle_coords and with parameters:

  • center - Tuple representing the center coordinates (x, y) in meters
  • radius - Radius of the circle in meters
  • speed - Speed of the end-effector in meters per second
  • time_var - Elapsed time in seconds
Figure 5: The circle the foot follows at a speed of 1 and of 3.

How precise you follow the trajectory depends on the speed you set. With low speeds you can track the circle perfectly. With larger speeds the system can't keep up and overshoots. This is due multiple reaseons like:

  • Inertia and Momentum: At higher speeds, the inertia and momentum of the robot leg increase, making it harder to change directions quickly and accurately.
  • Centrifugal and Coriolis Forces
  • Trajectory Planning and Execution - at higher speeds our trajectory has less points to create a full circle. This is due a fixed rate we send data to our motors eg. every 20ms.
  • Feedforward Control: Lack of proper feedforward control can lead to errors in trajectory tracking, as the controller might not anticipate the required accelerations and decelerations.

You can see that from the example with speed set to 1 and 3.

docs.title: Example code
docs.text:
This code will make your robot leg draw the above circles. It might look complicated but it is not. Once you understand how this example works you can use it as a base for building more complicated projects.

2DOF_leg_demo.py
import Spectral_BLDC as Spectral
import SourceRoboticsToolbox as SourceRoboticsToolbox
import time
import numpy as np
# We are using v1.1.0
from roboticstoolbox import DHRobot, RevoluteDH, ERobot, ELink, ETS
from math import pi, sin, cos
from spatialmath import *
from oclock import Timer, loop, interactiveloop
import math
from typing import Union, Any, List, Optional, cast
INTERVAL_S = 0.02

Needed_joint_pos = np.array([14000,2430]) # These are the positions we got from calib code
Joint_reduction_ratio = [1, 0.90476190] # Reduction ratio we have on our joints

# Setup your CAN coms. Change the channel to match your CAN adapter
Communication1 = Spectral.CanCommunication(bustype='slcan', channel='COM6', bitrate=1000000)

# Define our motors
Motor: list[Union[Spectral.SpectralCAN,Spectral.SpectralCAN]] = []
Motor.append(Spectral.SpectralCAN(node_id=0, communication=Communication1))
Motor.append(Spectral.SpectralCAN(node_id=1, communication=Communication1))

# Define the joints
Joint: list[Union[SourceRoboticsToolbox.Joint,SourceRoboticsToolbox.Joint]] = []
Joint.append(SourceRoboticsToolbox.Joint(encoder_resolution = 14, master_position=Needed_joint_pos[0], gear_ratio = Joint_reduction_ratio[0], offset = -np.pi/2, dir = 0))
Joint.append(SourceRoboticsToolbox.Joint(encoder_resolution = 14, master_position=Needed_joint_pos[1], gear_ratio = Joint_reduction_ratio[1], offset = 0, dir = 0))

timeout_setting = 0.001

initial = 0
initial_setup = [0,0]

testing = 5

# Initialize position values
position_values =  np.array([0.0,0.0])
Motor_values = np.array([0,0])
received_ids = [0,0]

# robot length values (metres)
l = [0.112, 0.1]

alpha_DH = [0,0]

# Create robot model using DH params
L1 = RevoluteDH(a=l[0],d = 0,alpha=alpha_DH[0])
L2 = RevoluteDH(a=l[1],d = 0,alpha=alpha_DH[1])
robot = DHRobot([L1,L2], name="Two link")

prev_pos = np.array([0,0])
speed_var = np.array([0,0])

def generate_circle_coords(center, radius, speed, time):
  """
  Generates x,y coordinates for a circle at a given time, considering constant speed.

  Args:
      center: Tuple representing the center coordinates (x, y) in meters.
      radius: Radius of the circle in meters.
      speed: Speed of the end-effector in meters per second.
      time: Elapsed time in seconds.

  Returns:
      Tuple containing the x and y coordinates in meters.
  """

  # Calculate angular displacement based on speed and time
  angular_displacement = speed * time

  # Use parametric equations for a circle to generate coordinates
  x = center[0] + radius * math.cos(angular_displacement)
  y = center[1] + radius * math.sin(angular_displacement)

  return (x, y)

def save_xy_data(filename, xy_data):
  """
  Saves a list of x,y coordinates to a text file.

  Args:
      filename (str): The name of the text file to save the data to.
      xy_data (list): A list of tuples containing x and y coordinates.
  """

  with open(filename, 'a') as file:
    for x, y in xy_data:
      file.write(f"{x},{y}\n")

# Example usage with update loop (adjust update_interval for your needs)
center = (-0.04, -0.17)
radius = 0.03
speed = 0.8
time_var = 0

# We are using oclock module to generate stable interval defined with INTERVAL_S
timer = Timer(interval=INTERVAL_S, warnings=False, precise=True)
while timer.elapsed_time < 1100000:

    t1 = time.perf_counter()
    #Motor[0].Send_Respond_Encoder_data()
    #Motor[1].Send_Respond_Encoder_data()
    Motor[0].Send_data_pack_1(Position = Needed_joint_pos[0],Speed = speed_var[0], Current = 0)
    Motor[1].Send_data_pack_1(Position = Needed_joint_pos[1],Speed = speed_var[1], Current = 0)

    # Handles data we get from the motors
    for i in range(1, 3):  # read up to 2 replies
        message, UnpackedMessageID = Communication1.receive_can_messages(timeout=timeout_setting)
        #print(f"unpack{i} is: {UnpackedMessageID}")

        # Check if UnpackedMessageID is not None 
        if UnpackedMessageID is not None:

            # Update received id index; meaning that we received response from that CAN ID
            received_ids[UnpackedMessageID[0]] = 1
            Motor[UnpackedMessageID[0]].UnpackData(message,UnpackedMessageID)
            #print(f"Motor {UnpackedMessageID[0]}, position is: {Motor[UnpackedMessageID[0]].position}")
            unwrapped_position_raw = Joint[UnpackedMessageID[0]].unwrap_position(Motor[UnpackedMessageID[0]].position)
            Motor_values[UnpackedMessageID[0]] = Motor[UnpackedMessageID[0]].position
            position_values[UnpackedMessageID[0]] =  Joint[UnpackedMessageID[0]].get_joint_position(Motor[UnpackedMessageID[0]].position)

            if initial_setup[UnpackedMessageID[0]] == 0:
                initial_setup[UnpackedMessageID[0]] = 1
                Joint[UnpackedMessageID[0]].determine_sector(Motor[UnpackedMessageID[0]].position)

    # Generate desired x,y coordinates with respect to time_var
    x, y = generate_circle_coords(center, radius, speed, time_var)

    # Create a matrix with those x,y coordinates
    T2 = SE3(x, y, 0)
    # Perform inverse kinematics (get joint data from x,y data)
    q1 = robot.ik_LM(T2, q0 = [-0.8,-1],mask = [1,1,0,0,0,0])
    Needed_joint_pos[0] = Joint[0].get_encoder_position(q1[0][0])
    Needed_joint_pos[1] = Joint[1].get_encoder_position(q1[0][1])  
    speed_var[0] = ((Needed_joint_pos[0] - prev_pos[0]) / INTERVAL_S)
    speed_var[1] = ((Needed_joint_pos[1] - prev_pos[1]) / INTERVAL_S)
    print(speed_var)
    prev_pos[0] = Needed_joint_pos[0]
    prev_pos[1] = Needed_joint_pos[1]
    # Process or visualize the generated coordinates (x, y)
    #print(f"Time: {time_var:.2f}s, Coordinates: ({x:.4f}, {y:.4f})")

    # Update time
    time_var += INTERVAL_S

    t2 = time.perf_counter()
    #print(f"total time is {t2-t1}")

    T = robot.fkine(position_values)
    xy = T.t
    #print(f"{xy[0]},{xy[1]}")
    xy_data = [(xy[0], xy[1])]  # Assuming xy is a single pair of coordinates
    # Save data to a txt file
    save_xy_data('my_data.txt', xy_data)
    #time.sleep(0.05)

docs.title: Plot data
docs.text:
Script that will plot the data of your leg:

plot_leg_data.py
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def plot_data(filename):
  """
  Plots data from a text file in the format:
  x1, y1
  x2, y2
  ...

  Args:
      filename (str): The name of the text file containing the data.
  """

  try:
    with open(filename, 'r') as file:
      data = file.readlines()

    x_data = []
    y_data = []
    for line in data:
      # Split the line based on comma (",")
      values = line.strip().split(',')

      # Check if there are exactly two values per line
      if len(values) != 2:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid line format in file '{filename}': {line}")

      try:
        x = float(values[0])
        y = float(values[1])
      except ValueError:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid data type in file '{filename}': {line}")

      x_data.append(x)
      y_data.append(y)

    # Ensure equal x and y scales
    plt.axis('equal')

    # Create the plot
    plt.plot(x_data, y_data)

    # Customize the plot (optional)
    plt.xlabel('X-Position')
    plt.ylabel('Y-Position')
    plt.title('Data Plot from ' + filename)

    plt.grid(True)
    plt.show()

  except FileNotFoundError:
    print(f"Error: File '{filename}' not found.")
  except (ValueError, TypeError) as e:
    print(f"Error: {e}")

# Example usage
filename = 'C:\\Users\\xx\\Desktop\\test_code\\env\\Robot_leg\\data_2.txt'  # Replace with your actual filename
plot_data(filename)

docs.title: SimpleFOC guide
docs.text:
Tested with Simple FOC@^2.3.2 release

Main firmware that runs on Spectral micro is Spectral firmware.

SimpleFOC is alternative to Spectral Firmware. The library is intended both for:

  • Beginners searching for a simple and user-friendly way to learn how to control BLDC and Stepper motors
  • Advanced users ready to dig deeper into the FOC algorithm and optimize the code for their particular application/hardware.

More info about simple FOC:

  • Forum
  • DOCS
  • Discord

SimpleFOC forum and discord is best place to look for help when developing with SimpleFOC library

docs.title: How to install
docs.text:
Follow this guide

This replaces the bootloader

This project has no upload offset, so an upload with the programming adapter writes SimpleFOC at 0x08000000, over the bootloader. Firmware updates over UART or CAN stop working. To go back to the Spectral firmware, install the bootloader again as in Installing the bootloader on an older board, then flash a release.

Your platformio.ini should look like this:

platformio.ini
[env:genericSTM32F103CB]
platform = ststm32
board = genericSTM32F103CB
framework = arduino
upload_protocol = stlink
build_flags = 
debug_tool = stlink
monitor_speed = 115200
lib_deps = 
    askuric/Simple FOC@^2.3.2
lib_archive = false

docs.title: Basic example
docs.text:
This example will spin the motor in open loop and enable serial monitor. Use this code as a base for more advanced code you will develop with SimpleFOC. The Spectral-Micro-Simple-FOC repository has this project and more examples in its examples folder, among them voltage-torque FOC with the encoder.

main.cpp
#include "Arduino.h"
#include "SimpleFOC.h"

// Driver PWM pins
#define PWM_CH1 PA_2
#define PWM_CH2 PA_1 
#define PWM_CH3 PA_0 

// Encoder pins
#define MOSI PB_5
#define MISO PB_4
#define CLK PB_3
#define CSN PA_15

#define SENSE1 PA_4 // Inline current sense
#define SENSE2  PA_3 // Inline current sense

#define TX_COM PB_6
#define RX_COM PB_7

// Current sense resistors
#define SENSE_RESISTOR 0.025f
#define CURRENT_AMP_GAIN 20

// Serial pins
#define Serial Serialx
HardwareSerial Serialx(RX_COM, TX_COM); // PA3, PA2 RX,TX

// BLDC motor & driver instance
// BLDCMotor motor = BLDCMotor(pole pair number, phase resistance (optional) );
BLDCMotor motor = BLDCMotor(11);
//  BLDCDriver3PWM( pin_pwmA, pin_pwmB, pin_pwmC )
BLDCDriver3PWM driver = BLDCDriver3PWM(PWM_CH1, PWM_CH2, PWM_CH3);

//target variable
float target_velocity = 0.1;

void Init_pins();

void setup() {  

  // Init driver enable pins and LED
  Init_pins();

  // pwm frequency to be used [Hz]
  driver.pwm_frequency = 20000;
  // power supply voltage [V]
  driver.voltage_power_supply = 24;
  // Max DC voltage allowed - default voltage_power_supply
  driver.voltage_limit = 5;
  // driver init
  driver.init();
    // link the motor and the driver
  motor.linkDriver(&driver);
  motor.controller = MotionControlType::velocity_openloop;

  // init motor hardware
  motor.init();
    // use monitoring with the BLDCMotor
  Serial.begin(115200);
  Serial.println("Motor ready!");
  _delay(1000);
  // monitoring port
  motor.useMonitoring(Serial);

}

void loop() {
  // open loop velocity movement
  // using motor.voltage_limit and motor.velocity_limit
  motor.move(target_velocity);
  // monitoring function outputting motor variables to the serial terminal 
  motor.monitor();

}

void Init_pins(){
  pinMode(PA_9, OUTPUT);
    pinMode(PA_8, OUTPUT);
    pinMode(PA_10, OUTPUT);
    pinMode(PB_15, OUTPUT);
    pinMode(PB_14, OUTPUT);
    pinMode(PB_13, OUTPUT);

  digitalWrite(PA_9,HIGH);
  digitalWrite(PA_8,HIGH);
  digitalWrite(PA_10,HIGH);
  digitalWrite(PB_14, HIGH);
  digitalWrite(PB_15, HIGH);
  digitalWrite(PB_13, HIGH);
}

docs.title: API reference
docs.text: Every CAN message and every UART command of the firmware release this site describes, the factory defaults of its settings and which of them are saved, the error flags, and the map from the Python library's calls to the messages they send.

docs.title: Where the facts come from
docs.text: The command IDs, the frame lengths the firmware accepts, the responses it sends, the list of UART commands with their kind (Set/Get, Get or action), their argument type, the mode each enters and what it prints, the parameter numbers, and the defaults are read from the firmware's source at its release tag by tools/sync_firmware.py in the documentation repository, and the pages are built from that at every build. The descriptions, units and byte layouts are written by hand, and the build fails when they name a command the firmware does not have, or miss one it has, or when a byte layout does not fit the frame. The firmware version is in the version box on the landing page.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Bytes are numbered from 0, the first byte on the bus (data[0]). Multi-byte values are big-endian: the most significant byte first. Floats are IEEE 754 single precision in 4 bytes.
  • Bits inside a byte are numbered from the most significant bit: bit 7 is the first flag the firmware packs into the byte, bit 0 the last.
  • Encoder ticks: 16384 per revolution; speeds in ticks per second; currents in mA; voltages in mV.
  • UART command names are case-sensitive and spelled exactly as the firmware compares them.

docs.title: In the API reference
docs.text:
• CAN protocol: the identifier, the three kinds of message, every message by group, and every parameter
  • UART commands: the syntax and every command by group
  • Defaults
  • Errors and LED states
  • Python library: library call → message

docs.title: CAN frame tool and downloads
docs.text: Build or inspect a frame using the command definitions of this manual's firmware release. All calculations run in your browser; the tool does not connect to an adapter or send commands to hardware.

docs.title: Downloads
docs.text:
Command definitions (JSON) · Position DBC · Velocity DBC · Current DBC

The JSON includes the firmware tag, source commit, message IDs, every documented layout and its bit order. The DBC files cover nodes 0 to 13, with both the clean and fault-bit identifiers of driver replies. Reserved commands are omitted. Values use the firmware's native units: ticks, ticks/s, mA and the units in the CAN reference.

Choose the DBC for the Send_data_pack_1 layout your host sends:

File Command layout Position DBC 8 bytes: position, speed feedforward, current feedforward Velocity DBC 5 bytes: speed, current feedforward Current DBC 2 bytes: current

The three layouts share a CAN identifier. DBC cannot select a layout from the frame's length, so load the matching file; the browser decoder below handles all three lengths. Other message layouts are the same in each download.

An RTR request uses the same identifier as its data reply. DBC describes the data reply; it does not represent the request's RTR flag or the empty gripper status poll. Both are supported by the browser tool.

The gripper's two object-detection bits have an unusual order: bit 5 is the low bit, bit 4 the high bit. The DBC signal gripper_object_detection_raw retains the wire value and supplies text labels (raw 2 = object while closing, raw 1 = object while opening). The browser decoder converts that pair to the firmware's numeric status (1 = closing, 2 = opening).

docs.title: Try a frame
docs.text:
The example 0x07A, data C8 1E 01 2C C0, is a command to gripper node 0: position 200, speed 30, current 300 mA, activate and action set, E-stop and release direction clear. These are an illustration of the encoding; the device's current and motion limits still apply. Select another message above the fields to build one of its documented forms. To inspect a reply, enter its identifier and data bytes below.

Loading the firmware's command definitions…

Build a frame Node ID (0–13) Message and layout Driver reply has an active fault (error bit 1) Build frame Use this frame in the decoder Decode a frame CAN identifier (hex) Data bytes (hex, up to eight) Remote request (RTR; no payload) Decode frame Enable JavaScript for the frame tool, or use the reference tables and downloads above.

Check

The example decodes to the values above. Change the identifier to 0x1FA to see the same command addressed to node 3. An invalid length or out-of-range field produces an explanation instead of a frame.

For wiring, termination, host timing and recovery, use Over CAN. To look up a message's purpose and accepted lengths, use the CAN reference.

docs.title: Defaults
docs.text:
The settings of the firmware, read from its source at the release this site describes. The table leaves out the firmware's internal state (counters, flags, scratch variables).

  • Start value is the value in the firmware's structures (common.h). At power-up the firmware loads the saved settings from the EEPROM over it, so for a setting that #Save keeps the start value only shows until the EEPROM is read.
  • After #Default is what the driver runs with after #Default, which writes the factory values to the EEPROM and loads them. A fresh board, and a board whose saved configuration fails its check at power-up, gets the same values.
  • Kept by #Save says whether the setting survives a power cycle. No means the driver starts with the start value again after every power-up.

#Default also erases the calibration; from firmware 109 it keeps a valid stored CAN node ID (existing_id in the table; 0 when none is stored); see Saving the configuration. A name after a value, such as 160 (CURRENT_BANDWIDTH_DEFAULT), is the constant in constants.h the value comes from. The settings of firmware 109 that are parameters, the anti-cogging and the encoder table among them, are in the parameter table with their defaults.

docs.title: The error flags
docs.text:
The flags as the firmware keeps them, the line #Error prints for each, and where each sits in the two bytes of Send_Respond_State_of_Errors (bits numbered from the most significant).

Flag #Error prints Byte, bit Raised when Error In error state! 0, 7 any of the flags below is set (also the error bit of every CAN identifier) temperature_error Temp error 0, 6 the thermistor reads above #Tlim or below −20 °C (with #Term 1) encoder_error Encoder error 0, 5 the magnet is not detected or the reading fails its check Vbus_error Vbus error 0, 4 the supply is below 9 V or above #Vmax (29 V after #Default); from firmware 109 a low supply is not checked in the first 500 ms after power-up Driver_error Drv error 0, 3 the MOSFET driver reported a fault on its fault pin: undervoltage, thermal shutdown or overcurrent. #Error also prints FAULT pin is LOW: the gate driver reports a fault while the fault output is still active Velocity_error Velocity error 0, 2 the measured speed exceeds 20,000,000 ticks/s (about 1220 revolutions per second), a fixed limit: a runaway or an encoder fault, not #Vlimit Current_error Current error 0, 1 never in this firmware; reserved ESTOP_error Received ESTOP command 0, 0 Send_ESTOP was received Calibrated (0) Not calibrated 1, 7 (1 = calibrated) the motor has not been calibrated Activated — 1, 6 the activated flag, not an error Watchdog_error Watchdog error 1, 5 the watchdog time passed without a motion command or an answered request over CAN wrong_product Wrong firmware for this board (product lock) 1, 4 from firmware 109: the firmware found the other product's stamp, or a calibration its product cannot make, at start-up; it drives nothing

Gripper mode has its own flags in Respond_Gripper_data_pack: a temperature error (the driver's temperature error), a timeout error (the driver's watchdog error: the CAN watchdog ran out) and an E-stop error; see the Gripper reference.

docs.title: Clearing
docs.text: #Clear and Send_Clear_Error clear every flag except Calibrated and go to idle; a flag whose cause persists is set again at once. While any flag is set the driver disables the motor, which coasts whatever #Brake says. The watchdog, E-stop and velocity errors clear and stay clear; the Vbus, encoder, driver and temperature errors come back until the cause is gone. Calibration clears the calibration error. A wrong product stays until the right firmware is flashed. Clearing a watchdog error also ends a watchdog hold or descend.

docs.text: The Spectral-BLDC package (Spectral-BLDC-Python, pip install Spectral-BLDC) has one method per CAN message in Spectral_BLDC.SpectralCAN, and Spectral_BLDC.CanCommunication for the bus. With Python shows how they are used.

The calls for the messages added in firmware 109 (Send_Parameter, Send_Get_Parameter, Send_Respond_Identity, Send_Respond_Telemetry, Send_Buffer_Read, Send_Cogging_Harmonic, Send_Cogging_Table, Send_Sound, Send_Samples), Send_Settings and Send_Brake_Coast for the idle behaviour, and the actions 'Coast' and 'Descend' of Send_Watchdog, come with library 1.21. It also adds calls built on the parameters, among them Send_Watchdog_Fallback, Send_Tool_ID, Send_Cogging_Mode, Send_Capture_Setup, Send_Capture_Trigger, Send_Histogram, Send_Cogging_Calibrate and Send_Encoder_Calibrate; the sound calls Send_Tone, Send_Sound_Stop, Send_Sound_Event, Send_Sound_Play, Send_Sound_Clear, Send_Samples_Play and Send_Samples_Stop on top of Send_Sound and Send_Samples; and the module Spectral_BLDC.music (note names, ringtone melodies, MIDI and WAV files as queue events and samples, see Sound).

The same release adds Spectral_BLDC.helpers, blocking functions that send a request and wait for the answer: get_parameter and set_parameter (which reads the value back), read_identity, read_telemetry, features, read_buffer, capture, wait_for_state (for the encoder table, the anti-cogging and other runs), and play_events and stream_samples for sound. They are for setting up and diagnostics, not for the inside of a fast control loop. The library's examples folder shows them at work: parameters_and_status.py, capture.py, calibration_features.py, watchdog.py and sound.py.

The same release is stricter about what it sends and reads:

  • Send_Parameter takes the value itself. Parameters 8 to 16 and 20 are sent as floats (Send_Parameter(16, 1500) is 1500 mA); every other parameter takes a whole number, and anything else raises ValueError.
  • A position or a speed that does not fit 24 bits, or a current that does not fit 16 bits, raises ValueError; 1.20 wrapped it round. Send_Voltage_Limit raises ValueError outside 0 to 60000 mV.
  • A node ID must be 0 to 15.
  • UnpackData ignores frames from other nodes, remote frames and extended frames.
  • Parameters 79, 80 and 84 to 87 read as unsigned numbers.
  • A send that fails returns False and is logged once.

docs.title: Receiving
docs.text:
CanCommunication.receive_can_messages(timeout) returns (message, ids): the raw python-can message and a tuple ids with node_id, command_id and error_bit from the identifier, or (None, None) after the timeout. SpectralCAN.UnpackData(message, ids) decodes the message into the object's attributes:

Message Attributes Respond_data_pack_1 position, speed, current Send_Respond_Encoder_data position, speed Send_Respond_Iq_data current Send_Respond_Temperature temperature Send_Respond_Voltage voltage Send_Respond_Device_Info HARDWARE_VERSION, BATCH_DATE, SOFTWARE_VERSION, SERIAL_NUMBER Send_Respond_State_of_Errors error, temperature_error, encoder_error, vbus_error, driver_error, velocity_error, current_error, estop_error, calibrated, activated, watchdog_error; from 1.21 also wrong_product Send_Respond_Identity (1.21 and newer) product_id, product_name, tool_id, firmware_version, identity_hardware_version, pole_pairs, identity_calibrated, identity_flags Send_Respond_Telemetry (1.21 and newer) temperature, voltage, the error flags as above, current Respond_Parameter (1.21 and newer) parameters[number] (floats for 8-16 and 20), unknown_parameter; tool_id and watchdog_fallback when those parameters come in Respond_Buffer_Data (1.21 and newer) capture[index], histogram[bin], cogging_harmonics[slot], cogging_table[index], encoder_table[index] Send_Respond_Kt Kt Respond_Gripper_data_pack gripper_position, gripper_current, gripper_activated, gripper_action_status, gripper_object_detection, gripper_temperature_error, gripper_timeout_error, gripper_estop_error, gripper_calibrated

Object detection in the library

Library 1.20 and older assemble gripper_object_detection with the two bits swapped relative to the firmware, so they report 1 where the gripper sends 2 (object detected while opening) and 2 where it sends 1 (object detected while closing); 0 and 3 are unaffected. 1.21 and newer read them right.

docs.title: CAN protocol
docs.text:
CAN 2.0, 1 Mbit/s, 11-bit identifiers. The identifier carries the node ID (bits 10 to 7, 0 to 15), the command ID (bits 6 to 1, 0 to 63) and, in frames from the driver, the error bit (bit 0). Over CAN explains how the pieces are used; this page lists them.

Three kinds of message:

  • Send_… — the host sends data to the driver. A few are answered (the motion commands with Respond_data_pack_1, the gripper command with Respond_Gripper_data_pack); most are not.
  • Send_Respond_… — the host asks for data with a remote frame (RTR bit set, no data) under the command ID; the driver answers with a data frame under the same command ID.
  • Respond_… — frames only the driver sends.

Multi-byte values are big-endian (data[0] first); floats are IEEE 754 single precision; bits inside a byte are numbered from the most significant bit (bit 7 first).

docs.title: By group
docs.text:
• Motion: the motion commands and their answers
  • Gains and limits: the loop gains, the limits, Kt
  • Status requests: temperature, voltage, device info, errors, current, encoder, Kt, identity, telemetry, the heartbeat
  • System: node ID, E-stop, idle, save, reset, clear, watchdog, heartbeat setup, settings
  • Parameters and buffers: the parameters behind Send_Parameter and Send_Get_Parameter, every one of them, and the buffers: capture, histogram, anti-cogging, encoder table
  • Sound: tones, the queue and samples through the motor
  • Gripper: the gripper command, calibration and the gripper state

docs.title: The Python library
docs.text: Every message the host can send has a method of the same name in Spectral_BLDC.SpectralCAN, listed in Python library.

docs.title: Tools and downloads
docs.text: Build or decode a CAN frame, and download this firmware's JSON and DBC definitions.

docs.title: Gains and limits
docs.text: The commands that set the loop gains and the limits. None of them is answered; save with Send_Save_config.

docs.title: Send_PD_Gains
docs.text:
ID 16host → driver8 bytesPython: Send_PD_Gains()

Sets KP and KD, the gains of the impedance (PD) loop. Keep them with Send_Save_config.

8 bytes

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0-3 KP float 32 4-7 KD float 32

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.text:
ID 17host → driver8 bytesPython: Send_Current_Gains()

Sets Kp and Ki of the PI current loop of Iq. The Id loop keeps its gains; over UART, #Kpiq and #Kiiq set both loops, and so do parameters 11 and 12.

8 bytes

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0-3 Kp_iq float 32 4-7 Ki_iq float 32

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Limits
docs.text:
ID 20host → driver8 bytesPython: Send_Limits()

Sets the speed limit and the current limit the loops may reach. From firmware 109 a negative value, or one that is not a number, is ignored, and the current limit stops at the driver's 2800 mA, as with #Ilim. Firmware 107 and older stored the current limit as it arrived. Never send more than the motor's rating.

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0-3 Speed limit float 32 encoder ticks/s 4-7 Current limit float 32 mA

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Gripper
docs.text: The commands of gripper mode (#Gripper 1, saved).

docs.title: Send_gripper_data_pack
docs.text:
ID 61host → driver0 or 5 bytesPython: Send_gripper_data_pack()

The gripper command, for a driver set up as a gripper (#Gripper 1, saved). Position, speed and the current limit of the move, plus the activate, action and E-stop bits. A move is carried out only while the gripper is calibrated, activated and the action bit is 1. An empty frame (0 bytes) only asks for the state.

5 bytes

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0 Position unsigned 8-bit 0 fully open, 255 fully closed 1 Speed unsigned 8-bit 0 slowest, 255 fastest 2-3 Current signed 16-bit current limit of the move in mA; from firmware 109 its magnitude is used and it stops at 2800 mA; see the gripper manual for the safe range 4 7 Activate bit 1 activate the gripper, 0 deactivate 4 6 Action bit 1 go to the position, 0 idle 4 5 E-stop bit 1 raises the gripper E-stop error 4 4 Release direction bit read by the firmware but not used

The driver answers with Respond_Gripper_data_pack.

docs.title: Send_gripper_calibrate
docs.text:
ID 62host → driver0 bytesPython: Send_gripper_calibrate()

Starts the gripper calibration (the jaws find their end stops). Needed after every power-up.

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Respond_Gripper_data_pack
docs.text:
ID 60driver → host4 bytes

The driver's answer to Send_gripper_data_pack: position, measured current, and the state bits. Python attributes gripper_position, gripper_current, gripper_activated, gripper_action_status, gripper_object_detection, gripper_temperature_error, gripper_timeout_error, gripper_estop_error, gripper_calibrated. The Python library 1.20 and older combine the two object-detection bits the wrong way round, so their gripper_object_detection reads 2 for an object found while closing and 1 for one found while opening; 1.21 and newer read them as the table says.

The frame (4 bytes)

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0 gripper_position unsigned 8-bit 0 fully open, 255 fully closed 1-2 gripper_current signed 16-bit measured current in mA 3 7 gripper_activated bit 1 activated 3 6 gripper_action_status bit the action bit of the last Send_gripper_data_pack (1 after #Grippos); the driver never clears it, so it stays 1 after the move ends: the object detection tells when the move has ended 3 5-4 gripper_object_detection 2 bits bit 5 is the low bit, bit 4 the high bit: 0 moving, 1 object detected while closing, 2 object detected while opening, 3 at the position 3 3 gripper_temperature_error bit the driver's temperature error 3 2 gripper_timeout_error bit the driver's watchdog error: the CAN watchdog ran out 3 1 gripper_estop_error bit 3 0 gripper_calibrated bit 1 calibrated

docs.title: Motion
docs.text: The commands that move the motor and the frames that come back.

docs.title: Send_data_pack_1
docs.text:
ID 2host → driver2 or 5 or 8 bytesPython: Send_data_pack_1()

The motion command. Its length decides the control mode the driver enters: 8 bytes command a position with a speed and a current feedforward, 5 bytes a speed with a current feedforward, 2 bytes a current. Send 0 for a feedforward you do not use. A frame of any other length is ignored (the driver flags it as a wrong data length) but still answered.

8 bytes — position setpoint with speed and current feedforward (position mode)

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0-2 Position setpoint signed 24-bit encoder ticks 3-5 Speed feedforward signed 24-bit encoder ticks/s 6-7 Current feedforward signed 16-bit mA

5 bytes — speed setpoint with current feedforward (velocity mode)

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0-2 Speed setpoint signed 24-bit encoder ticks/s 3-4 Current feedforward signed 16-bit mA

2 bytes — current setpoint (current mode)

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0-1 Current setpoint signed 16-bit mA

The driver answers with Respond_data_pack_1.

Every form resets the watchdog. With Rstint set, the integral accumulators are cleared on each new setpoint. From firmware 109 a position or speed frame that follows another mode (idle, current, PD, a watchdog trip) starts the velocity integral from zero, so a release from a wound-up mode does not kick; one that follows position or velocity mode keeps it. The new setpoint, the mode change and the driver's wake-up reach the control loop together, so the first frame after Idle is followed.

docs.title: Send_data_pack_PD
docs.text:
ID 4host → driver8 bytesPython: Send_data_pack_PD()

Puts the driver in impedance (PD) mode and sets the position, speed and current feedforward of the PD loop, whose gains are KP and KD (Send_PD_Gains).

8 bytes

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0-2 Position setpoint signed 24-bit encoder ticks 3-5 Speed setpoint signed 24-bit encoder ticks/s 6-7 Current feedforward signed 16-bit mA

The driver answers with Respond_data_pack_1.

Firmware 106 and older wrote the speed into the feedforward instead of the PD loop's speed setpoint, so the speed term had no effect; 107 fixed it.

docs.title: Respond_data_pack_1
docs.text:
ID 3driver → host8 bytes

The driver's answer to Send_data_pack_1 and Send_data_pack_PD: where the motor is, how fast it turns and the current it draws. The Python library stores them as position, speed and current.

The frame (8 bytes)

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0-2 position signed 24-bit encoder ticks 3-5 speed signed 24-bit encoder ticks/s 6-7 current signed 16-bit Iq in mA

docs.text:

Reserved. The firmware has no handler for this ID and the Python library's call does nothing.

docs.title: Send_data_pack_3
docs.text:
ID 8host → drivernot implemented

Reserved. The firmware has no handler for this ID and the Python library's call does nothing.

docs.text:
ID 5driver → host0 bytes

Reserved; the driver never sends it.

ID 7driver → host0 bytes

docs.title: Parameters and buffers
docs.text:
From firmware 109 a setting that has no command of its own is a parameter: a number from 1 to 89 behind one pair of commands, Send_Parameter (ID 36) to set it and Send_Get_Parameter (ID 37) to read it, answered with Respond_Parameter (ID 38). The identifier has room for only 64 command IDs, so new settings no longer use them up. Parameter numbers are permanent: a number is never given a new meaning. Number 73 is not used and stays free. Parameters 84 to 87 are read only and say which build and which board answer: the git commit the firmware was built from (84), its build time in Unix seconds (85), the board ID (86) and the calibration ID (87). #Info prints them as Build, Board ID and Calibration ID (Status and diagnostics). Parameters 88 and 89, a diagnostic of when the current sensors are read, are the Spectral Micro's own; STEPFOC does not have them.

The buffers are the larger data a drive holds: a capture of three signals, a histogram, the anti-cogging set and the encoder table. Send_Buffer_Read (ID 41) reads them in 8-byte frames, Respond_Buffer_Data (ID 42) carries them, and Send_Buffer_Write (ID 43) writes the anti-cogging set.

Over UART, #Par does the same: #Par lists every parameter, #Par 1 reads one, #Par 1,200 sets it (Status and utility).

docs.title: Setting and reading a parameter
docs.text:
A set is not answered: read the value back to know what the driver took. A value outside a parameter's range is clamped, replaced or refused, as the table says, and a read-only number ignores the write.

import Spectral_BLDC as Spectral

comms = Spectral.CanCommunication(bustype='slcan', channel='COM41', bitrate=1000000)
motor = Spectral.SpectralCAN(node_id=0, communication=comms)

motor.Send_Parameter(1, 200)               # tool id 200, a custom tool
motor.Send_Get_Parameter(1)                # read it back
message, ids = comms.receive_can_messages(timeout=0.1)
if message is not None:
    motor.UnpackData(message, ids)
print(motor.parameters.get(1))
motor.Send_Save_config()                   # keep it over a power cycle

Send_Parameter, Send_Get_Parameter and the buffer calls need the Spectral-BLDC library 1.21 or newer. Send_Parameter takes the value itself: a gain or a limit (8 to 16 and 20) is sent as a float, so motor.Send_Parameter(16, 1500) sets a current limit of 1500 mA; every other parameter takes a whole number.

docs.title: Send_Parameter
docs.text:
ID 36host → driver5 bytesPython: Send_Parameter()

Sets one parameter by its number (the parameter table). Firmware 109 gives new settings a parameter number instead of a command ID of their own, since the identifier has room for only 64 command IDs. A value outside a parameter's range is clamped, replaced or refused as the table says; a number the firmware does not know, or a read-only one, is ignored. The driver does not answer: read the value back with Send_Get_Parameter. A value set this way lives in RAM until Send_Save_config, like every other setting; the table says which parameters Save keeps.

5 bytes

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0 Parameter unsigned 8-bit the parameter number, 1-87 1-4 Value signed 32-bit the new value, in the parameter's unit; for the gains, limits and Kt (8-16, 20) a float's bit pattern

The driver does not answer this command.

A data frame of another length, or a remote frame, is ignored and flagged as a wrong data length. It does not reset the watchdog.

docs.title: Send_Get_Parameter
docs.text:
ID 37host → driver1 bytesPython: Send_Get_Parameter()

Asks for the value in force of one parameter. The answer, Respond_Parameter, comes under ID 38, not 37: a host and a driver must never send data frames with the same identifier, because two sent at the same moment collide. Resets the watchdog. The Python library stores the value in parameters[number].

1 bytes

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0 Parameter unsigned 8-bit the parameter number

The driver answers with Respond_Parameter.

docs.title: Respond_Parameter
docs.text:
ID 38driver → host5 bytes

The answer to Send_Get_Parameter: the number and the value in force. For a number the firmware does not know the frame carries the number alone (1 byte; the Python library sets unknown_parameter). The gains, limits and Kt (parameters 8 to 16 and 20) travel as the bit pattern of an IEEE-754 float, the others as integers.

The frame (5 bytes)

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0 parameter unsigned 8-bit the parameter number 1-4 value signed 32-bit the value in force; a float's bits for 8-16 and 20

docs.title: Send_Buffer_Read
docs.text:
ID 41host → driver5 bytesPython: Send_Buffer_Read()

Asks for entries of one of the drive's buffers: the capture, the histogram, the anti-cogging harmonics or table, or the encoder table. The driver answers with one Respond_Buffer_Data frame per entry (for the two tables, one per three values), sent from its main loop whenever a transmit mailbox is free, so a long read-out never holds up the control loop or other answers. A new request replaces one still in progress; count 0 cancels it. Entries past the end are not sent. Resets the watchdog.

5 bytes

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0 Kind unsigned 8-bit 0 capture (up to 1024 samples: parameter 32 says how many), 1 histogram (256 bins), 2 anti-cogging harmonics (8 slots), 3 anti-cogging table (256 values), 4 encoder table (128 values) 1-2 First unsigned 16-bit the first index 3-4 Count unsigned 16-bit how many entries; 0 cancels a read-out

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Respond_Buffer_Data
docs.text:
ID 42driver → host8 bytes

One entry of a buffer, the answer to Send_Buffer_Read. The first two bytes say which: the kind in the top three bits, the index in the other thirteen (kind × 8192 + index). The six bytes after them depend on the kind, as the table below the frame says.

The frame (8 bytes)

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0-1 header unsigned 16-bit kind × 8192 + index 2-3 word_a signed 16-bit capture: channel A; histogram: the count (unsigned); harmonics: the harmonic number (0 = slot unused); tables: entry index 4-5 word_b signed 16-bit capture: channel B; histogram: the sum's upper 16 bits; harmonics: a, the cosine term in mA; tables: entry index + 1 6-7 word_c signed 16-bit capture: channel C; histogram: the sum's lower 16 bits; harmonics: b, the sine term in mA; tables: entry index + 2 (0 past the end) Kind Index Bytes 2-7 0 capture the sample, oldest first, 0 to parameter 32 − 1 channels A, B and C, each in its signal's unit (the parameter table lists the signals) 1 histogram the bin, 0-255 over one electrical turn or one motor turn the count (unsigned 16-bit), then the sum (signed 32-bit); the bin's mean is sum ÷ count 2 anti-cogging harmonics the slot, 0-7 the harmonic of the electrical angle (1-32, 0 = unused), a and b in mA: the slot adds a·cos(h·θ) + b·sin(h·θ) 3 anti-cogging table the first of three values, 0-255 three values in mA, 64 angle counts apart (256 per electrical turn) 4 encoder table the first of three values, 0-127 three corrections in 1/16 encoder count, 128 per motor turn

docs.title: Send_Buffer_Write
docs.text:
ID 43host → driver8 bytesPython: Send_Cogging_Harmonic(), Send_Cogging_Table()

Writes the anti-cogging set: kind 2 one harmonic slot per frame, kind 3 three table values per frame, in the Respond_Buffer_Data layout. Other kinds are ignored (the encoder table cannot be written), and so is a harmonic above 32. The set lives in RAM until Send_Save_config; switch it on with parameter 37. The driver does not answer.

8 bytes

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0-1 Header unsigned 16-bit kind × 8192 + index; kind 2 or 3 2-3 Word A signed 16-bit kind 2: the harmonic (1-32, 0 = unused); kind 3: value at index 4-5 Word B signed 16-bit kind 2: a in mA; kind 3: value at index + 1 6-7 Word C signed 16-bit kind 2: b in mA; kind 3: value at index + 2

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Every parameter
docs.text: The number and the name are read from the firmware; the rest is checked against its source. Access: a read-only parameter ignores a write; a run parameter starts or stops a run when written and gives its state when read.

docs.title: Watchdog and tool
docs.text:
Parameters 1 to 5 live in settings block 2 of the EEPROM, 6 and 7 in the first settings block beside the other settings; Send_Save_config keeps all seven. A value outside a range is clamped, replaced or ignored, as the Value column says.

No. Name Access Value Kept by Save What it is 1 PARAM_TOOL_ID set, read 0 none, 1 SSG-48, 11-33 MSG, 200-254 your own tools; a value outside 0-255 is ignored. Default 0 yes, settings block 2 What the drive is built into. For an MSG the tens digit is the rail (1 = 100, 2 = 150, 3 = 200 mm) and the units digit the stepper (1 = 21.5, 2 = 40, 3 = 60 mm). Also #Tool; reported in the identity frame. 2 PARAM_WD_FALLBACK_TIME set, read ms, 0-60000 (clamped). Default 2000 yes, settings block 2 How long watchdog hold or descend runs before the after-action takes over. 3 PARAM_WD_FALLBACK_CURRENT set, read mA, signed, -32768 to 32767 (outside: 0). Default 0 yes, settings block 2 The current watchdog descend applies. 0 lets gravity lower a joint; a gripper gets its grip current. 4 PARAM_WD_FALLBACK_SPEED set, read ticks/s, 0-65535 (outside: 1000). Default 1000 yes, settings block 2 The speed watchdog descend never exceeds, in either direction. 5 PARAM_WD_AFTER_ACTION set, read 0 legacy, 2 brake, 3 coast (any other value: 0). Default 0 yes, settings block 2 What follows hold or descend when the fallback time has run out. 6 PARAM_WD_TIME set, read ms, 0 = off (a negative value: 0). Default 0 yes, settings block 1 The watchdog time, the same value Send_Watchdog sets. 7 PARAM_WD_ACTION set, read 0 legacy, 1 hold, 2 brake, 3 coast, 4 descend (outside 0-255: 0; 5-255 act as legacy). Default 0 yes, settings block 1 What a trip of the watchdog alone does, the same value as byte 4 of Send_Watchdog.

Parameter 23, the product stamp, stays read only.

Stamped at the first start-up of a calibrated board and at every save. A firmware that finds the other product's stamp drives nothing (see Errors).

docs.title: Current sensing and the current loop
docs.text:
The current-sense zero is the ADC reading with no current flowing, in counts from 2048 (1 count is about 1.6 mA). The driver measures it at every start-up with the bridge off; the trim is added to it.

No. Name Access Value Kept by Save What it is 21 PARAM_SENSE1_OFFSET set, read counts from 2048, -400 to 400 (outside: refused) no: measured again at every start-up The current-sense zero of channel 1 in use. Measured at start-up (the trim, 59, added); writable for tests, until the next start-up. 22 PARAM_SENSE2_OFFSET set, read counts from 2048, -400 to 400 (outside: refused) no: measured again at every start-up The current-sense zero of channel 2 in use, as 21. 40 PARAM_SENSE1_OFFSET_OFF read only counts from 2048 no: measured at every start-up The zero of channel 1 measured with the bridge off, the trim added. 41 PARAM_SENSE2_OFFSET_OFF read only counts from 2048 no: measured at every start-up The zero of channel 2 measured with the bridge off, the trim added. 42 PARAM_SENSE_ZERO_SWITCHING read only 0 not run, 1 measuring, 2 in use, 3 rejected (implausible), 4 interrupted (a command or an error came first), 5 measured, not in use no The second zero measurement, made in idle after start-up with the bridge switching at 50 % duty. On the bench it made the current ripple worse, so it is measured and kept but not used unless 46 asks for it. 46 PARAM_SENSE_ZERO_USE_SWITCHING set, read 1 the zero measured with the bridge switching, 0 the bridge-off zero. Default 0 no Which zero is in use. 1 takes effect only while 42 reads 5 (measured, not in use). 47 PARAM_SENSE1_OFFSET_SW read only counts from 2048 no The zero of channel 1 measured with the bridge switching. 48 PARAM_SENSE2_OFFSET_SW read only counts from 2048 no The zero of channel 2 measured with the bridge switching. 49 PARAM_CURRENT_BANDWIDTH set, read Hz, 10-500 (outside, or with R or L not set: refused). 160 at every start-up no; the gains it sets are kept by Save Writing it sets Kp_iq and Ki_iq at once from R, L and this bandwidth, as #Cbw does. Reading gives the bandwidth the gains in force amount to with the R and L in force (0 without them). 58 PARAM_ID_SETPOINT set, read mA, -3000 to 3000 (outside: refused). Default 0 no The d-axis current setpoint, as #Id. It makes no torque, only more current in the coils. 59 PARAM_ZERO_TRIM1 set, read counts, -60 to 60 (outside: refused). Default 0 yes, encoder block The trim added to the zero of channel 1 measured at every start-up; writing it moves the zero in use at once. The Spectral Micro firmware 109 skips the trim step of the anti-cogging identification, so only a write sets it. 60 PARAM_ZERO_TRIM2 set, read counts, -60 to 60 (outside: refused). Default 0 yes, encoder block The trim of channel 2, as 59. 61 PARAM_THETA_OFFSET read only 0.1° electrical yes, with the calibration The electrical offset between the encoder and the motor, found by calibration (#Offset in rad). 62 PARAM_TRIM_H1_BEFORE read only 0.1 mA no The 1st harmonic of the anti-cogging set found by an identification with the trim (43 = 4 or 5). 63 PARAM_TRIM_H1_AFTER read only 0.1 mA no After a trim, the 1st harmonic again; the Spectral Micro skips the trim, so it equals 62. 64 PARAM_COMM_DELAY_US set, read µs, 0-500 (outside: refused), 0 = off. Default 234 no: 234 at every start-up Commutation delay compensation: the output voltage is turned forward by the angle the rotor covers in this time. Applied in the closed-loop modes above 100 ticks/s. 234 µs is the Spectral Micro's own delay, measured on the bench. 65 PARAM_FAST_TRIG set, read 1 from the integer sine table, 0 from the float routine. Default 0 no Where the transforms of every control loop take sin and cos from. On the STEPFOC bench the table was not faster. 88 PARAM_SENSE_SAMPLE_AT set, read -1: read wherever the code is (the default); 0 to the PWM period (the timer's reload value): wait for that count first (outside: refused) no: -1 at every start-up An experimental diagnostic of when the current sensors are read, off by default. They are read by a software start, wherever the code happens to be in the 25 kHz centre-aligned PWM cycle, so the moment of a reading depends on the code before it. With a count set, the driver waits until the PWM counter is within 24 counts of it (at most about 60 µs), then reads. Leave it at -1 unless you are investigating the current sensing. 89 PARAM_SENSE_SAMPLE_SEEN read only the PWM counter at the last reading, +65536 while it counts down — Where in the PWM cycle the last current reading happened; it shows where parameter 88 puts the readings.

docs.title: What is in force: parameter 79
docs.text:
Parameter 79 says in one read what the drive runs with. #Info prints the same at its end, under In force:. Bit 0 is the least significant.

Bit Set when 0 the motor is calibrated 1 an encoder table is measured (in RAM) 2 the encoder table is in use (parameter 53) 3 an anti-cogging set is in RAM (harmonics or table) 4 anti-cogging is on (parameter 37 not 0) 5 anti-cogging is on as the table (otherwise as the harmonics) 6 the anti-cogging set in RAM is the one saved in the EEPROM 7 a current-sense zero trim is applied (parameter 59 or 60 not 0) 8 the current-sense zero measured with the bridge switching is in use (parameter 46) 9 commutation delay compensation is on (parameter 64 not 0) 10 the speed estimate is a PLL (parameter 50 is 1 or 2) 11, 12 0 on the Spectral Micro (the STEPFOC's fast reading and fast PWM) 13 sin and cos come from the integer table (parameter 65) 14 the position input filter is on (parameter 74 not 0) 15 the velocity-integral deadband is on (parameter 75 not 0) 16-17 parameter 56 (no effect on the Spectral Micro) 20 a calibration is running 21 the encoder table is being measured 22 the anti-cogging is being identified 23 the runs after a calibration are about to start 24 sound is playing (Sound)

Bits 18, 19 and 25 to 31 are 0.

docs.title: Reading the capture
docs.text:
A capture records three signals inside the control loop, one sample every divider loops, 1024 samples per channel. It starts when parameter 28 is written: at once (1), when the error flag rises (2, a watchdog trip included), or when channel A rises (3) or falls (4) through the level of parameter 29. Parameter 30 keeps that many samples from before the trigger. Status and diagnostics shows a whole capture.

  1. Set the signals (24, 25, 26), the divider (27), the pre-trigger (30) and, for 3 and 4, the level (29).
  2. Write the trigger (28). Parameter 31 reads 1 (armed), 2 (recording), then 3 (done).
  3. Read parameter 32 (samples readable) and 33 (the trigger sample's index, −1 if none).
  4. Send_Buffer_Read with kind 0, first 0, count = parameter 32: one Respond_Buffer_Data frame per sample, oldest first.

The histogram works the same way with parameters 34 to 36 and kind 1: it adds a signal into 256 bins by the electrical angle or by the encoder, every control loop, until it is stopped or one bin holds 65535 samples.

docs.title: Sound
docs.text: Sound through the motor: tones, a queue of timed events and samples, added to the output voltage while the driver holds or moves. Sound explains how to use them; parameters 80 to 82 are in the parameter table.

docs.title: Send_Sound
docs.text:
ID 44host → driver8 bytesPython: Send_Sound()

Plays sound through the motor: a tone now, a queue of timed events, or samples. The sound is added to the output voltage, on the q axis by default (parameter 82), and only while the driver holds or moves (position, velocity, current or PD mode); idle or an error stops all of it. Up to 4 tones sound at once (channels 0 to 3), from 20 Hz to below 2500 Hz, half the control-loop rate. Loudness is given as a current: the driver turns it into a voltage with the coil's impedance at that pitch, so low and high notes sound alike. The total voltage is limited to parameter 81 (2000 mV by default; 0 refuses sound). Added in firmware 109. The driver does not answer; parameter 80 says what plays. The Python library wraps the operations as Send_Tone, Send_Sound_Stop, Send_Sound_Event, Send_Sound_Play, Send_Sound_Clear, Send_Samples_Play and Send_Samples_Stop.

8 bytes

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0 Operation unsigned 8-bit 0 stop everything (tones, queue, samples); 1 a tone now; 2 add an event to the queue; 3 play the queue; 4 play the samples; 5 samples off, buffer cleared; 6 clear the queue (tones that sound keep sounding) 1 Channel unsigned 8-bit the tone channel, 0-3 (operations 1 and 2) 2-3 A unsigned 16-bit 1, 2: the pitch in Hz (2: 0 silences the channel); 4: the sample rate in Hz, at most the loop rate 4-5 B unsigned 16-bit 1, 2: the loudness in mA; 4: the voltage of a full-scale sample in mV 6-7 C unsigned 16-bit 1: the duration in ms, 0 = until stopped; 2: the wait in ms before the next event, 0 = the next one starts with it

The driver does not answer this command.

The queue holds 31 events and is played by the control loop with loop-exact timing: an event sets one channel's pitch and loudness, then waits. A chord is three events with wait 0 and a fourth with the chord's length. When the queue runs out, every channel falls silent. An event sent to a full queue is dropped. Samples: send them first with Send_Sound_Samples, then operation 4; the driver plays them at the given rate and stops when the buffer runs dry. A frame of another length, or a remote frame, is ignored. It does not reset the watchdog.

docs.title: Send_Sound_Samples
docs.text:
ID 45host → driver1 to 8 bytesPython: Send_Samples()

Appends 1 to 8 samples (signed 8-bit, one per byte, −127 to 127 = full scale) to the driver's 1024-place sample buffer, which holds 1023 samples. Samples that do not fit are dropped; parameter 80 says how many are buffered. Send_Sound with operation 4 plays them. Added in firmware 109. The driver does not answer.

8 bytes — eight samples; a shorter frame carries fewer

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0 Sample 1 signed 8-bit the next sample 1 Sample 2 signed 8-bit 2 Sample 3 signed 8-bit 3 Sample 4 signed 8-bit 4 Sample 5 signed 8-bit 5 Sample 6 signed 8-bit 6 Sample 7 signed 8-bit 7 Sample 8 signed 8-bit

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Respond_Device_Info
docs.text:
ID 25host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frameremote frame, 0 bytesPython: Send_Respond_Device_Info()

Asks for the driver's identity: hardware version, batch date and serial number from the EEPROM, and the firmware release (from firmware 105 on this is the build's own version; before, a value from the EEPROM).

The frame (7 bytes)

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0 HARDWARE_VERSION unsigned 8-bit PCB revision 1 BATCH_DATE unsigned 8-bit production batch, the lowest 8 bits of the stored value (24092024 after #Default is sent as 120) 2 SOFTWARE_VERSION unsigned 8-bit firmware release, e.g. 107 3-6 SERIAL_NUMBER unsigned 32-bit serial number

The driver answers with Send_Respond_Device_Info.

docs.title: Send_Respond_State_of_Errors
docs.text:
ID 26host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frameremote frame, 0 bytesPython: Send_Respond_State_of_Errors()

Asks for every error flag and the calibrated, activated, watchdog and product-lock states.

The frame (2 bytes)

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0 7 error bit any error is active 0 6 temperature_error bit motor over the temperature limit 0 5 encoder_error bit magnet not detected or misaligned 0 4 vbus_error bit supply voltage outside the limits 0 3 driver_error bit the MOSFET driver reports undervoltage, thermal shutdown or overcurrent 0 2 velocity_error bit speed over the limit 0 1 current_error bit reserved; never set by this firmware 0 0 estop_error bit Send_ESTOP was received 1 7 calibrated bit the motor is calibrated 1 6 activated bit the controller is activated 1 5 watchdog_error bit the watchdog ran out 1 4 wrong_product bit from firmware 109: this firmware is on the other product's board (the product lock) and drives nothing

The driver answers with Send_Respond_State_of_Errors.

docs.title: Send_Respond_Iq_data
docs.text:
ID 27host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frameremote frame, 0 bytesPython: Send_Respond_Iq_data()

Asks for the measured Iq current.

The frame (2 bytes)

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0-1 current signed 16-bit mA

The driver answers with Send_Respond_Iq_data.

docs.title: Send_Respond_Encoder_data
docs.text:
ID 28host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frameremote frame, 0 bytesPython: Send_Respond_Encoder_data()

Asks for the position and the filtered speed, as 32-bit values. Python attributes position and speed.

The frame (8 bytes)

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0-3 position signed 32-bit encoder ticks 4-7 speed signed 32-bit encoder ticks/s

The driver answers with Send_Respond_Encoder_data.

docs.title: Send_Respond_Kt
docs.text:
ID 33host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frameremote frame, 0 bytesPython: Send_Respond_Kt()

Asks for the torque constant Kt the driver uses. Added in firmware 104.

The frame (4 bytes)

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0-3 Kt float 32 Nm/A

The driver answers with Send_Respond_Kt.

docs.title: Send_Respond_Identity
docs.text:
ID 39host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frameremote frame, 0 bytesPython: Send_Respond_Identity()

Asks what the drive is: the product, the tool it is built into, the firmware release, the hardware version, the pole pairs, whether it is calibrated, and eight flags. A host can check it before it commands or flashes a drive. Added in firmware 109. Python attributes product_id, product_name, tool_id, firmware_version, identity_hardware_version, pole_pairs, identity_calibrated, identity_flags.

The frame (8 bytes)

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0 product unsigned 8-bit 1 STEPFOC, 2 Spectral Micro: the firmware that answers 1 tool_id unsigned 8-bit parameter 1: 0 none, 1 SSG-48, 11-33 MSG, 200-254 your own 2-3 firmware_version unsigned 16-bit the release, e.g. 109 4 hardware_version unsigned 8-bit PCB revision from the EEPROM 5 pole_pairs unsigned 8-bit the motor's pole pairs; 0 if outside 0-255 6 calibrated unsigned 8-bit 1 calibrated, 0 not 7 0 gripper bit the driver is set up as a gripper (#Gripper 1) 7 1 brake_on_idle bit idle brakes (1) or coasts (0) 7 2 commutation_reversed bit calibration found the coils wired the other way round 7 3 settings_block2 bit the EEPROM has the bank settings block 2 lives in, so parameters 1-5 can be saved 7 4 wrong_product bit this firmware is on the other product's board (the product lock) and drives nothing 7 5 sense_zero_measured bit the current-sense zero was measured at start-up and is plausible 7 6 cogging_saved bit the anti-cogging in use is the one saved in the EEPROM 7 7 switching_zero_in_use bit the current-sense zero measured with the bridge switching is in use (parameter 46)

The driver answers with Send_Respond_Identity.

The flags in byte 7 are numbered the usual way, bit 0 the least significant (unlike the error bytes, which the firmware packs from bit 7 down).

docs.title: Send_Respond_Telemetry
docs.text:
ID 40host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frameremote frame, 0 bytesPython: Send_Respond_Telemetry()

Asks for the temperature, the supply voltage, both error bytes and the current in one frame, all from the same moment: one request instead of four. Added in firmware 109. The Python library fills the same attributes as the four separate answers.

The frame (8 bytes)

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0-1 temperature signed 16-bit °C (meaningful with the thermistor enabled) 2-3 voltage signed 16-bit supply voltage in mV 4 errors_1 unsigned 8-bit the error flags, as byte 0 of Send_Respond_State_of_Errors 5 errors_2 unsigned 8-bit calibrated, activated, watchdog, wrong product, as byte 1 of Send_Respond_State_of_Errors 6-7 current signed 16-bit Iq in mA

The driver answers with Send_Respond_Telemetry.

docs.title: Respond_Heartbeat
docs.text:
ID 9driver → host0 bytes

The frame the driver sends on its own at the heartbeat interval (Send_Heartbeat_Setup); empty. Off by default. Any other frame the driver sends resets the heartbeat timer, so a driver that answers motion commands at a high rate never sends a heartbeat.

The frame (0 bytes)

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning

docs.title: System
docs.text: Identity, saving, resetting, errors, the watchdog, the heartbeat and the settings.

docs.title: Send_CAN_ID
docs.text:
ID 11host → driver1 bytesPython: Send_CAN_ID()

Gives the driver a new node ID, 0 to 13 (the firmware accepts up to 15, but the bootloader reserves 14 and 15: a driver on one of those cannot be updated over CAN). The driver answers to the new ID at once. The ID is kept over a power cycle only after Send_Save_config, and saving is also what copies it into the bootloader's board ID.

1 bytes

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0 ID unsigned 8-bit 0 to 13 (14 and 15 are accepted but reserved by the bootloader)

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_ESTOP
docs.text:
ID 0host → driver0 bytesPython: Send_ESTOP()

Stops the motor and raises the E-stop error, which stays until Send_Clear_Error.

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Idle
docs.text:
ID 12host → driver0 bytesPython: Send_Idle()

Puts the driver in idle mode: the motor coasts, or brakes when Send_Settings or #Brake 1 asked for it.

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Save_config
docs.text:
ID 13host → driver0 bytesPython: Send_Save_config()

Writes the current configuration (gains, limits, calibration, CAN ID, heartbeat, watchdog, gripper flag) to the EEPROM, and copies the CAN ID into the bootloader's board ID. From firmware 109 it also writes the tool id and the watchdog fallback (settings block 2), the anti-cogging set with its mode and scale, and the encoder table with its on/off flag, parameter 56 and the current-sense zero trims, each block with its own checksum; of the two large blocks only the 16-byte pages that changed are written. Not kept: the idle behaviour of Send_Settings, the current loop bandwidth, and every parameter the parameter table marks as not kept. A drive stopped by the product lock writes nothing.

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Reset
docs.text:
ID 14host → driver0 bytesPython: Send_Reset()

Resets the driver. From firmware 104 the reset lands in the bootloader, which waits 2 s for a flashing host and then starts the firmware again; this is how a firmware update begins.

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Clear_Error
docs.text:
ID 1host → driver0 bytesPython: Send_Clear_Error()

Clears the error flags and goes to idle; it also ends a watchdog hold or descend. An error whose cause is still present comes straight back. A calibration error is cleared only by calibrating.

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Watchdog
docs.text:
ID 15host → driver5 bytesPython: Send_Watchdog()

Sets the watchdog. The motion commands (Send_data_pack_1, Send_data_pack_PD, Send_gripper_data_pack) and the requests the driver answers (the Send_Respond_ remote frames, Send_Get_Parameter, Send_Buffer_Read) reset it; the other frames (Send_Parameter among them) and UART commands do not. When the time runs out the driver reports a watchdog error and does what the action byte says. 0 turns it off (the default). From firmware 109 the driver acts on the action byte, but only when the watchdog is the only active error: any other error gets the legacy response, the motor disabled and coasting. Hold and descend run for the fallback time (parameter 2, 2 s by default), then the after-action (parameter 5); they start only if the driver was in position, velocity, current, PD or gripper mode, otherwise the driver gives the legacy response and the motor coasts. Setting the time starts a fresh window, and a negative time means off. The watchdog explains each action. The setting is kept by Send_Save_config. The same values are parameters 6 and 7, which #Par reaches over UART: to turn off a saved watchdog, send 0 over CAN or #Par 6,0, and save.

5 bytes

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0-3 Time unsigned 32-bit ms; 0 = off 4 Action unsigned 8-bit 0 legacy (the motor disabled, coasting), 1 hold the position, 2 brake (not current-limited), 3 coast, 4 descend at the fallback current and speed; other values act as 0

The driver does not answer this command.

Firmware 107 and older store the action byte without acting on it. The Python library sends all five actions from 1.21 ('Idle', 'Hold', 'Brake', 'Coast', 'Descend'); 1.20 and older send only 0, 1 or 2.

docs.title: Send_Heartbeat_Setup
docs.text:
ID 30host → driver4 bytesPython: Send_Heartbeat_Setup()

Sets the heartbeat interval in ms; 0 turns the heartbeat off (the default). Kept by Send_Save_config.

4 bytes

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0-3 Interval unsigned 32-bit ms; 0 = off

docs.title: Send_Settings
docs.text:
ID 35host → driver2 bytesPython: Send_Settings()

Sets boolean settings that have no command of their own: a mask byte says which settings the frame touches, a value byte gives their new values; settings outside the mask are left alone. Bit 0 is the idle behaviour: 1 brake (phases shorted), 0 coast (the default). The setting is not saved: the driver coasts again after a power cycle. Braking applies only in idle without an error; an error always disables the motor, which then coasts. The braking current is not limited, see Control modes. Added in firmware 107 (STEPFOC 107). The Python library has Send_Settings(mask, value) and, for this bit, Send_Brake_Coast(brake) from 1.21; 1.20 and older have no call for it.

2 bytes

Byte Bit Field Type Meaning 0 Mask unsigned 8-bit bit 0 = write the idle behaviour 1 Value unsigned 8-bit bit 0: 1 brake, 0 coast

The driver does not answer this command.

docs.title: Send_Cyclic_command
docs.text:
ID 29host → drivernot implemented

Reserved. The firmware has no handler for this ID and the Python library's call does nothing.

docs.title: UART commands
docs.text: Every command the firmware release this site describes understands over the serial port. The kind, the argument type, the mode a command enters and what it prints are read from the firmware; the descriptions are written by hand. Over UART explains the protocol.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
#<Name> [number]
  • A Set/Get command sets the value when a number follows and prints the current value either way.
  • A Get command only prints.
  • An Action command does something; a number after it is ignored.
  • Names are case-sensitive, at most 19 characters; the argument is one word of at most 19 characters, without spaces, so a list is written with commas (#WdFb 2000,0,1000,2, #Par 1,200); firmware 107 and older allowed 20 characters for name and number together. The line ends with LF (CR before it is fine). 256000 baud, 8N1, 3.3 V.
  • A name the firmware does not know is answered Unknown command.

docs.title: By group
docs.text:
• Motion: setpoints and modes
  • Gains and limits: the loop gains, the limits, the integrator reset, the current loop bandwidth
  • Calibration and motor parameters: Cal and Calonly, the motor's R, L and pole pairs, the constants calibration finds, the calibration settings, the encoder table (Encal) and the anti-cogging (Cogcal)
  • Status and utility: save, reset, defaults, identity, errors, temperature, the cyclic output, any parameter (Par), the tool id, the watchdog fallback, the product lock
  • Gripper: gripper mode

docs.title: Calibration and motor parameters
docs.text: Command Kind Argument What it does Response #R Set/Get float: resistance in Ω The phase resistance of the motor, measured by Cal; it can also be set by hand. Also parameter 76, in mΩ. the current value #L Set/Get float: inductance in H The phase inductance of the motor, measured by Cal; it can also be set by hand. Also parameter 77, in µH. the current value #Kt Set/Get float: Nm/A The torque constant, found by calibration. the current value #KV Set/Get float: rpm/V The velocity constant, found by calibration. the current value #Flux Set/Get float: Wb The flux linkage, found by calibration. Works over UART from firmware 109; the parser of 107 and older accepted only the lowercase #flux, which had no handler. the current value #Calonly Action The calibration alone: like Cal, but nothing follows it. Save afterwards with Save. Added in firmware 109. Enters idle mode. the calibration log #Cal Action Runs the calibration routine (see Calibration): it measures R and L, finds the pole pairs, the phase order and the angle offset, and measures Kt, KV and the flux linkage. It uses its own 1600 mA current limit for its steps; from firmware 109 it puts the limit that was in force back when it ends. From firmware 109, when it succeeds, the encoder table and then the anti-cogging follow by themselves, and everything is saved (about a minute; keep the shaft free). Enters idle mode. the calibration log #Calonly Action The calibration alone: like Cal, but nothing follows it. Save afterwards with Save. Added in firmware 109. Enters idle mode. the calibration log #Offset Set/Get float: angle in rad The angle offset between encoder zero and electrical zero, found by calibration. the current value #Iqoffset Set/Get int: current in mA The current used by the angle-offset search and the commutation check of Cal, 300 mA by default. Not saved. the current value #Magnet Get Reads the encoder's magnet status. Magnet Good or Magnet Bad #Dir Set/Get int: 0 or 1 The base direction of the encoder and phase mapping. Calibration always sets it to 1 (0 after #Default); the direction it finds is the commutation direction, which #Info prints. the current value #Phase Get Prints the phase order found by calibration. Phase order is: N #Resv Set/Get int: voltage in mV The voltage the resistance test of Cal starts at; it rises until the power reaches Calpwr. Not saved. the current value #Calpwr Set/Get float: power in W The power the resistance and inductance tests of Cal may dissipate in the motor. Not saved. the current value #Openv Set/Get int: voltage in mV The voltage of the open-loop spin, in calibration and with Openloop. Not saved. the current value #Opens Set/Get float: electrical speed in rad/s The speed of the open-loop spin in calibration; the same setting as the speed of #Openloop. the current value #Vp Set/Get int: voltage in mV The voltage of the phase-order search in calibration. Not saved. the current value #Encal Set/Get nothing, or save, all, stop, on, off, state The encoder table (see Encoder table and anti-cogging). Alone it measures the table and uses it: the field turns the rotor open loop one shaft turn each way at 2048 ticks/s, about 20 s, with the shaft free. save also saves; all then identifies the anti-cogging and saves both; stop aborts; on and off switch the correction (on only with a measured table, and not while a run turns the motor); state or any other word only prints. The same as parameters 52 and 53. Added in firmware 109; not yet tested on a Spectral Micro. Encoder table: <state>, then the table's error in degrees #Cogcal Set/Get nothing, or save, trim, stop, state The anti-cogging identification on the drive (see Encoder table and anti-cogging): one motor turn forward and one back in velocity mode at parameter 44's speed (1500 ticks/s, about 22 s), the shaft free to turn. save also saves; stop aborts, also the encoder part of a combined run; state or any other word only prints. trim identifies like the plain command on the Spectral Micro: its firmware skips the current-sense trim. Added in firmware 109; not yet tested on a Spectral Micro. Anti-cogging identification: <state>, the speed and the identified cogging in mA rms, and the harmonics when done #Calibrated Set/Get int: 0 or 1 The calibrated flag. #Calibrated 1 clears a calibration error without calibrating; the motor may still be uncalibrated. the flag #PP Set/Get int: pole pairs The motor's pole pairs, found by Cal; they can also be set by hand. Also parameter 78: 1-49, only while idle (50 and more would read as a STEPFOC calibration); from 109 #PP answers PP: not taken (1-49, and only while idle) otherwise. the current value
