docs.title: Status and utility
docs.text: Command Kind Argument What it does Response #Vmax Set/Get int: voltage in mV The supply voltage above which a Vbus error is raised: 29000 mV after #Default. Vmax in mV: N #Save Action Writes the configuration to the EEPROM. Do it after calibration and after tuning. Save #Reset Action Resets the driver. From firmware 104 the reset lands in the bootloader, which waits 2 s for a flashing host and then starts the firmware again. nothing #Tlim Set/Get int: temperature in °C The temperature at which the temperature error is raised; 75 by default. Temp limit N #Default Action Writes the factory defaults to the EEPROM and loads them: the calibration is erased (Not calibrated), the gripper flag, heartbeat and watchdog are cleared, the hardware version and batch date are set to 1 and 24092024, and 1111 is stored as the serial number; from firmware 109 also the tool id (0), the watchdog fallback, and the anti-cogging set, the encoder table, its trims and parameter 56 (cleared). From firmware 109 the CAN node ID is kept (0 only when no valid one is stored). Note the values first. Loaded default config! #Temp Get Prints the thermistor temperature. °C, or Temp Off while the thermistor is disabled #Term Set/Get int: 0 or 1 Enables the thermistor measurement and the temperature error (off by default). the setting #Mode Get Prints the control mode. In voltage-torque mode (#Uq) it prints nothing. Idle mode, Position control, Speed control, Current control, PD control, Open loop, Gripper mode, Gripper calib mode #Vbus Get Prints the supply voltage. mV #Error Get Prints which errors are active. No errors! or In error state!, then one line per active error (see Errors and LED states), and FAULT pin is LOW: the gate driver reports a fault while the driver stage's fault pin is active #Clear Action Clears the errors and goes to idle. An error whose cause is still present comes straight back; a calibration error is cleared only by calibrating (or #Calibrated 1). Enters idle mode. Clear errors #Iabc Get Prints the phase currents. Ia, Ib, Ic in mA #PWM Get Prints the PWM duty values. the duties #Help Action Prints a short command reference. Added in firmware 106. the reference #Info Action Prints the driver's identity and the motor: hardware version, batch date, firmware version, ISR time, CAN ID, calibrated or not, temperature, Vbus, Dir, phase order, commutation direction, the speeds of the calibration spin, pole pairs, R, L, Kt and KV. From firmware 109 also the build (Build:, the git commit, with + when built with uncommitted changes), the Board ID (this board, from the chip's unique number; not the bootloader's board ID), the Calibration ID (new at every successful calibration), the CAN receive overruns and dropped transmits, the product, the current-sense zeros, the tool id, the watchdog and its fallback, settings block 2, the anti-cogging, and at the end the In force: section (see Status and diagnostics). The serial number is #SERNUM, the gains #Param, the errors #Error. the report #Tool Set/Get int: 0 to 255 The tool id: what the drive is built into, 0 none, 1 SSG-48, 11-33 MSG (tens = rail ½/3 = 100/150/200 mm, units = stepper ½/3 = 21.5/40/60 mm), 200-254 your own. The same as parameter 1. Kept by Save. Added in firmware 109. Tool ID: N, or Invalid tool id (0-255) #Tone Set/Get f,mA[,ms], or off A tone through the motor (see Sound): #Tone 440,250,1000 plays 440 Hz at a loudness of 250 mA for 1000 ms, on the axis parameter 82 picks. mA left out: 200; ms left out: 500; ms 0: until #Tone off. 20 Hz up to below 2500 Hz. It plays only while the driver holds or moves; from idle a calibrated driver first holds the position it is at (#Idle releases it). #Tone alone or #Tone off stops all sound. Added in firmware 109. Enters position mode. Tone 440 Hz, 250 mA, 1000 ms; from idle first Holding the position while it plays (#Idle releases it); Tone: not played (…) when it cannot; Tone off #Par Set/Get int: n, or n,value Any parameter by its number (see Parameters and buffers): alone it lists every parameter, #Par 1 reads one, #Par 1,200 sets it (no spaces); a gain or limit (8-16, 20) takes a decimal, e.g. #Par 9,0.02 sets Kpv. Added in firmware 109. P<n> = <value>; refused: out of range, read only, not now, or unknown when the driver did not take it; P<n> unknown #Product Action nothing, or claim, clear The product lock: prints this firmware and the board's stamp. claim stamps the board as this product (a repaired board, a motor the stamp rule misjudges), clear removes the stamp; power-cycle after either. Over UART only. Added in firmware 109. Firmware: Spectral Micro; board stamp: … #WdFb Set/Get int list: time_ms,current_mA,speed_ticks_s,after_action The watchdog fallback, four numbers at once without spaces, e.g. #WdFb 2000,0,1000,2: how long hold or descend runs, descend's current and speed cap, and what follows (0 legacy, 2 brake, 3 coast). The same as parameters 2 to 5, clamped the same way; fewer than four numbers change nothing. Kept by Save. Added in firmware 109. Watchdog fallback: … ms, … mA, … ticks/s, then … #Param Get Prints every gain of every loop. the gains #Cyc Set/Get int: interval in ms (0 = off) Sends position, speed and Iq on its own every interval: $ <position> <speed> <Iq>; for BetterSerialPlotter. Cyclic disabled for #Cyc without a number; #Cyc 0 stops the output without an answer #Cyca Set/Get int: interval in ms (0 = off) Like Cyc, in the Arduino plotter format Position:x,Speed:y,Iq:z. Cyclic disabled for #Cyca without a number; #Cyca 0 stops the output without an answer #CANID Set/Get int: 0 to 13 The CAN node ID. Use 0 to 13: the firmware accepts 14 and 15, but the bootloader reserves them and a driver on one of those cannot be updated over CAN. Kept over a power cycle after Save, which also copies it into the bootloader's board ID; from firmware 109 Default and a settings reset keep it too. the ID, or Invalid CAN ID #SERNUM Set/Get int: number The serial number. Save writes it to the EEPROM, but the firmware does not read it back at power-up: after a power cycle the driver reports 1. Serial number is: N #Activate Action Sets the controller's activated flag (bit 6 of byte 1 of Send_Respond_State_of_Errors). It is not the gripper's activate bit, which #Gripact and Send_gripper_data_pack set. Controller activated #Pullconfig Get Prints the whole configuration on one line, for Motor GUI. the configuration #LED Set/Get int: 0 or 1 Turns the status LED on or off. the LED state

docs.title: Getting help
docs.text:
• Questions and discussion: the Source Robotics Discord.
  • A problem with the driver or the firmware: an issue in the firmware repository; see Report a problem for what to include.
  • A mistake on a page of this site: every page ends with a link to edit it and one to report it; see Contributing.
  • Orders and hardware: source-robotics.com.

Before you ask, Troubleshooting goes through the common symptoms, and #Info tells most of what anyone will ask you for.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: This documentation lives in Source-Robotics/Spectral-BLDC-docs. A small fix can be made from the browser: the Edit it on GitHub link at the end of every page opens the page's source, and GitHub turns your change into a pull request. For anything larger, open an issue first.

docs.title: How the site is built
docs.text:
• The pages are Markdown, built with MkDocs and the Material theme; the repository's README.md says how to preview it locally.
  • The site describes one firmware release, named in versions.yml. The command IDs, frame lengths, the UART command list and the defaults in the Reference are read from the firmware's source at that release's tag by tools/sync_firmware.py; do not edit those facts in the pages. The descriptions of the commands are in docs/includes/can_commands.yml and uart_commands.yml.
  • Every push runs a strict build (a broken link fails it) and the tool tests. A push to main publishes the site under its firmware version with mike.

docs.title: House rules
docs.text:
• Facts come from the firmware. When a page and the firmware disagree, the firmware is right; fix the page, or report the firmware.
  • Spell commands exactly as the firmware does, even where the spelling looks wrong.
  • Write for someone who has the driver in front of them and wants to do one thing: say what to do, in order, then why.
  • Three kinds of boxes: a note, a notice (damage) and a danger (injury). Use them for those, not for emphasis.
  • Images: under 2400 px on the long side, with a caption that says what the reader should see.

docs.title: Licence
docs.text: Text and images: CC BY-SA 4.0: copy, adapt and share them, also commercially, if you credit Source Robotics and share your changes under the same licence. Code: the MIT licence, which covers the code examples in the pages and the site's own code. The Source Robotics name, the product names and the logos are not covered by either. By contributing you agree that your contribution is published under these licences.

docs.title: Report a problem
docs.text:
Open an issue in the firmware repository for the driver and its firmware, or in Spectral-BLDC-Python for the Python library. Include:

  1. The output of #Info, #Error and #Param, copied from the terminal. They carry the hardware and firmware version, the motor parameters, the calibration state, the errors and the gains.
  2. The motor: type, and the resistance, inductance and pole pairs calibration found (#Info prints them).
  3. The supply: voltage, and whether it has a current limit.
  4. What you did and what happened: the commands, in order, and the driver's answers; the calibration log if it is about calibration.
  5. How it is wired: a photo of the board on the motor and of the cables helps more than a description.

For a problem with this documentation, the Report it link at the end of the page opens an issue in the documentation repository with the page already named.
